thread:
incident-bot: PAGED: P1 - hosted-runtime kv-cache OOM spike in us-west-2 - paging oncall. Investigate immediate mitigation. link: https://redwood/pager/2119800000 :rotating_light:

sarah.k: acknowledging, I'm oncall. seeing repeated OOMs on a subset of hosted runtime shards. memory climbs steadily during long prompt sessions and then OOMs the kvcache process.

devon.m: can you paste the tail of the runtime logs? any stack traces or eviction logs?

sarah.k: logging snippet below. looks like continuous-batching + prefetch kicked in and kvcache grew without bounds for some sessions.

sarah.k: ```
[2026-03-15T12:03:41Z] runtime: shard=usw2-a instance=rt-prod-7 kvcache: prefetch queued for sess=xxxx seq=0..8192 estimated_entries=120000 memory=18.2GB
[2026-03-15T12:03:41Z] runtime: shard=usw2-a instance=rt-prod-7 batching: window_expand to 32 -> active_batches=48
[2026-03-15T12:04:12Z] runtime: shard=usw2-a instance=rt-prod-7 kvcache: entries=1.1M mem=42.9GB evictions=0
[2026-03-15T12:04:42Z] runtime: shard=usw2-a instance=rt-prod-7 kvcache: OOM: process killed by OOM (rss 86GB)
```

priya: ugh. that matches the regression we rolled two days ago (continuous-batching change + prefetch heuristic tweak). Iirc we enabled larger window expansion to improve throughput.

jordan: confirmed. rollback candidate: revert the window expansion patch (pr 4521) and temporarily disable kv prefetch for hosted.

eng-runtime-oncall: agree with rollback + kill prefetch on the fleet. we can push a runtime flag to disable prefetch on hosted-prod quickly. will need coord with deploy-bot.

sarah.k: customer-impact check: latency seems fine for short requests, but customers with very long prompts (chat transcripts > 50k tokens) experienced request failures and some 500s. I'm seeing ~24 customer-visible errors in last 30 mins, mostly in us-west-2. No billing anomalies reported yet.

customer-success: flagged 3 paying customers on a support thread; they're seeing generation failures mid-stream. asking for ETA on mitigation.

devon.m: steps I'd take right now:
1) disable kvcache prefetch on hosted via runtime feature flag (fast, no churn)
2) scale down batch window target (from 32 to 8) via rollout config to reduce kvcache pressure
3) if necessary, revert pr 4521 and roll back the batching change
4) re-run health checks and monitor memory metrics

eng-runtime-oncall: I'm drafting the change. quick patch: set KV_PREFETCH_ENABLED=false and BATCH_WINDOW_MAX=8 for hosted-prod. will push to canary then global.

sarah.k: please also add a temporary alert rule to escalate when kvcache_mem > 30GB on any shard. existing thresholds were tuned for smaller windows.

eng-runtime-oncall: deploying canary now. deploy-bot: `deploy runtime/hosted flags --env prod --shard usw2-a --flags KV_PREFETCH_ENABLED=false,BATCH_WINDOW_MAX=8`

deploy-bot: Started rollout to shard usw2-a (canary) - build runtime-flags-20260315-cc3

sarah.k: canary stats: within 3 minutes memory plateaued and then dropped; no OOMs on canary shard. error rate for long-prompt sessions on that shard dropped to 0.

priya: great. once canary looks stable for 10m, roll out to remaining us-west-2 shards. keep prefetch disabled until we have a tested prefetch cap.

jordan: action item: cut a short-lived hotfix branch that caps prefetch per-session to 8 entries and adds a hard memory guard for kvcache. mark as revert-safe.

devon.m: note for post-incident: we should add per-session kv entry quotas and tighten the prefetch heuristic to account for predicted token length from the prompt header. also instrument prefix amplification patterns.

customer-success: relaying ETA: we'll tell customers ~20-30min for mitigation rollouts; will follow up when global rollout completes.

eng-runtime-oncall: rolling to rest of usw2 now. deploy-bot: rolling to shards usw2-b,c,d,e with flags.

deploy-bot: rollout 40%...70%...100% - complete.

sarah.k: post-rollout checks: memory usage back to baseline across usw2, no new OOMs in the last 12 minutes. total customer 500s in window: 31, most aligned with timeframe before canary.

priya: logging decision: keep prefetch disabled on hosted for 6 hours, then enable a conservative mode (per-session cap 8) behind a feature flag and monitor. create a follow-up ticket to ship a robust mitigation in 2 weeks.

jordan: assigning follow-up to eng-runtime team: RUNTIME-8472. add owners: devon.m, priya.

eng-runtime-oncall: handing off to next oncall (sarah.k -> jordan). Jordan, see the runbook link: https://redwood/runbooks/kvcache-ooms and the mitigation diffs: https://redwood/changeset/4521-hotfix

jordan: taking handoff. summary: P1 resolved via runtime flags disabling prefetch and shrinking batch window. customer impact: transient 500s for long prompts in us-west-2 (~31 customers affected), support notified. follow-ups: RUNTIME-8472 (prefetch cap & heuristics), RUNTIME-8473 (alerts tuning), RUNTIME-8474 (postmortem).

sarah.k: leaving notes: timeline + logs saved in incident doc https://redwood/incidents/2119800000. I added heap samples and flamegraphs to the attachment list.

customer-success: customers updated. will reopen if they see regressions. thanks all. :heart:
